record.count_text: the delivery loop and network progression (33)

clauses.text: The board at any terminal is therefore not a list of templates but a reading of the valley: what this station can spare, who among the places you know is short of it, how badly, how far
what the walk asks (wading, scrappers, deep grey, steep, or "river — needs a crossing")
and what your pack will weigh after you say yes
A station never posts an order for a need it is thriving on
Stock sets a mood — critical < 15, wanting < 35, steady < 65, thriving

figure.note: shelves at 12, 25, 50 and 70 read critical, wanting, steady and thriving — inside the bands, not at their edges (economy.mjs walks the edges)

clauses.text: mood sets the price: ×2.2

figure.note: the card, the slip's row and the pay for a town out of what it needs

clauses.text: Haven makes tools and textiles
Weight and capacity (Hauling, packs, companions) decide how many orders one trip can chain
The gold Guide line under the compass always says what to do next, which key does it, and where it is
M1 tap on a terminal, ruin, crate, cairn, paver, pylon or event — walk there and use it
A delivered crate adds 28
Several crates landed in one trip pay a rising chain bonus (+15% per further stop
a core delivered puts a station on the wire
and the connection cinematic names who will feed whom
its light pushes back the grey and pacifies camps it reaches
Lit land burns the veil off entirely and takes a warm gold wash
the mechanics of light (safety, regen, pacification, coverage)
The map draws the same overlay, so territory reclaimed is territory brightened
Connecting a station repaints both the field and the map in the cinematic's expanding ring
When a station is connected, what its connected neighbours make flows to it on its own (0.06/s per feeding maker)

figure.note: a minute of the valley moves 0.06 a second from each lit maker, to within 0.05 of a shelf point

clauses.text: Stock for each need sits on a 0–100 bar that drains with time (0.035/s × population; the unconnected ration at half rate)

figure.note: each shelf's minute is the wire's flow less 0.035 × its people; the Quarry off the wire at half

clauses.text: The player is told this the first time it happens
its goods move to its neighbours on their own
more than its people consume, so a connected pair sustains itself and its stock climbs to full
the connected core saturates and stops posting; the frontier is where the crates are needed
The wire pushes the player outward
auto-travel skirts scrapper territory when you are loaded (×5 path cost)

figure.note: the loaded planner's ring round Pass Camp is read present, then gone; its cost is not read

clauses.text: Roads are speed on foot and wire throughput
A paved road between two stations multiplies that flow (×1.6 partial

figure.note: one stretch of the Elm Road's two paved carries ×1.3 — a partial road adds by the share paved, under the ×1.6 a partial road approaches (the record does not say which it meant)

clauses.text: roads and routes widen the wire
Porters are mortal, the network is immortal (PZ)
stations, stars, stock, roads, structures, banked materials, reputation, hired waylighters and route charters persist across deaths
class, traits, skills, equipment and cargo die with the body — recoverably
the delivery loop
network progression
